land.text: 'the governorates of Volyn, Kiev, Podillia, Chernihiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, Katerynoslav, Kherson and Taurida (except of Crimea)' named in the Third Universal of 20 November 1917

predecessors.note: UPR page infobox: 'Preceded by Russian Republic (1917)' and 'Autonomy within the Russian Republic (1917-1917/1918)'.

land.text: the Ukrainian land held by the Bolsheviks after the collapse of the UPR; the page's infobox: 'Succeeded by Ukrainian SSR (1919)'

the western Ukrainian lands left to Poland when 'the Polish government signed the Peace of Riga' on 18 March 1921 (the Civil War page: it 'split disputed territories in Belarus and Ukraine between Poland and Soviet Russia/Soviet Ukraine')

successors.note: The region is my reading: no page opened names the lands Poland kept.

capitals.name: Kyiv (Kiev)
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Kiev, with temporary de facto capitals 'Kamianets-Podilskyi; Vinnytsia; Zhmerynka; Proskuriv; Rivne' (no years given). The page also says Kyiv fell to the Bolsheviks on 5 February 1919 and that the Ukrainian army re-entered it on 1 March 1918; the years of the other seats are not given.

union.text: Polesia: the former Pinsk, Mozyr and Rechitsa uezds, centred on Mozyr

correction.text: Ukraine east of the Zbruch without 'West Ukraine, Budjak and Crimea': the Third Universal's nine governorates (Volyn, Kiev, Podillia, Chernihiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, Katerynoslav, Kherson, Taurida except Crimea) and, for the Ukrainian State of 1918, also Kholm governorate and Polesia ('the former Pinsk, Mozyr and Rechitsa uezds')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has nothing for 1917-1918. 'covered most of the territory of modern-day Ukraine, with the exception of most of West Ukraine, Budjak and Crimea. Its territory, however, extended into today's Russia, Belarus, Moldova and Poland.' Only the Polesia strip is placed; Kholm governorate (Chelm land in Poland) and the Russian border strips toward Kursk and Voronezh are named on the page but not placed here. Crimea was 'dependent on Ukraine' with 'negotiations ... for its direct accession' (page) and is left out. The page gives no area for the State. [Reviewer eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: Crimea subtracted from the correction to match its text and the UPR page's 'Taurida (except of Crimea)'.]

522,688 km2. The infobox gives 860,000 km2 (undated, a claim), ratio 0.61: inside the factor of two. The shape is Ukraine east of the Carpathians with Eastern Galicia (175 of 198 gazetteer cells) and Volhynia (247 of 292), without Crimea, Transcarpathia, Bukovina and most of Budjak: it matches the claim after the Unification Act with the West Ukrainian People's Republic ('on 22 January the two states officially united'), not the land the Directorate held. Kyiv fell to the Bolsheviks on 5 February 1919, so effective control was far smaller for most of the year; no page opened maps the 1919 front (unverified: page budget), which is why the ledger now carries loss events for the Bolshevik gains of January-March 1919 and for Eastern Galicia (July 1919) and keeps the contest only for the Volhynia-Podillia front. [Reviewer-fix eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: verdict ok changed to adjust (shape unchanged): the claim stood only from the union of 22 January to the Bolshevik advances that month and the next; between this shape and the 1920 keyframe the land falls by about 90 percent and is now explained by the loss events of 1919. The fall of Volhynia (Poles took Lutsk on 15 May 1919 and 'soon occupied southwestern Volhynia', UPR page; the Treaty of Warsaw in April 1920) has no event of its own: the pages give no extent.]

correction.text: The shape is unchanged: Cliopatria's 1919 polygon is the claim after the Unification Act of 22 January 1919, held in full only in early 1919. The ledger takes the land away: Soviet gains of January-March 1919 and Poland's of Eastern Galicia on 18 July 1919.
the towns the page lists as the republic's temporary de facto capitals ('Kamianets-Podilskyi; Vinnytsia; Zhmerynka; Proskuriv; Rivne'), each with a 60 km radius

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, deliberately small: Cliopatria's 1919 shape ends with 1919 and the page gives no map of 1920-21. After the April 1920 Treaty of Warsaw the UPR's army fought beside Poland and the republic ended at the Peace of Riga (18 March 1921), 'the republic's government continued its activities in exile'. The radius around the capitals is my reading of the infobox (Zhmerynka and Proskuriv are covered by Vinnytsia and Khmelnytskyi); confidence 1 as a territory. [Reviewer-fix eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: the Kiev offensive page supports the small pocket: before the offensive of 25 April 1920 the UPR 'controlled only a small sliver of land near the territory administered by Poland' (no map or extent on the page); Polish forces had taken Kamianets-Podilskyi by 16 November 1919 and 'the Polish authorities allowed the UPR to establish its official state structures there'. The four-circle pocket stays a reading of the capitals (confidence 1).]

region.text: the nine governorates the Third Universal named, Crimea excepted

ledger.note: 1917, 20 November (7 November O.S.): the Central Rada's Third Universal proclaims the Ukrainian People's Republic, still as autonomy 'within the Russian Republic'. The page: the Universal was 'adopted on 20 November 1917 (7 November by Old Style)' and named 'the governorates of Volyn, Kiev, Podillia, Chernihiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, Katerynoslav, Kherson and Taurida (except of Crimea)'. [Reviewer eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: Crimea subtracted from the region, as the page's Third Universal names Taurida '(except of Crimea)'.]

region.text: the former Pinsk, Mozyr and Rechitsa uezds, the Polisia okruha centred on Mozyr

ledger.note: 1918: Ukraine takes Polesia at Brest-Litovsk. The page: 'Ukraine had gained ownership of the territory of the former Pinsk, Mozyr and Rechitsa uezds' (Brest-Litovsk section; no month).

region.text: Kyiv and its surroundings, taken by the Red Army in the winter of 1918

ledger.note: 1918, January: the Bolsheviks take Kyiv from the Rada. The Civil War page: 'the Bolsheviks captured the city on 26 January'; the UPR page ties the fall to the day the Brest-Litovsk treaty was signed (9 February), so the day differs by two weeks between pages.

1918, January: Bolshevik forces take the left bank and the Dnieper bend. The Ukrainian-Soviet War page: 'Yekaterinoslav (January 9), Aleksandrovsk (January 15), and Poltava (January 20)'; the UPR page agrees on 9 January (Katerynoslav) and 20 January (Poltava). Mirror of ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic /ledger/1; the land returns with the Brest-Litovsk gain of 3 March.

1918, 9 February: Muravyov's Bolshevik forces take Kyiv. The Ukrainian-Soviet War page: they 'entered Kiev under Mikhail Muravyov's on February 9'; the UPR page: the treaty with the Central Powers 'was signed on the day of Kyiv's fall to the Red Army'. The Russian Civil War page puts the capture at 26 January, which is why the contest below starts in January. Mirror of ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic /ledger/2; the Ukrainian army re-enters on 1 March.

region.text: Ukraine, whose independence the Fourth Universal had declared on 22 January 1918

ledger.note: 1918, 3 March: Soviet Russia gives up Ukraine at Brest-Litovsk. The page: 'Russia renounced all territorial claims in Finland' and 'Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, most of Belarus, and Ukraine'; the Central Powers had already recognised the republic in the night of 8-9 February. [Reviewer eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: Crimea subtracted from the region, as the page's Third Universal names Taurida '(except of Crimea)'.]

1918, 1 March: the Ukrainian army returns to Kyiv. The page: 'on 1 March 1918 the Ukrainian army under command of K. Prisovsky and S. Petliura entered Kyiv', with German forces arriving 'several days later'.

1918, 29 April: Skoropadsky's coup turns the republic into the Ukrainian State (Hetmanate). The page: 'Established: 29 April 1918'; the Ukrainian State page describes 'a congress of the League of Landowners consisting of some 6,500 delegates' at which Skoropadsky 'was elected the Hetman of all Ukraine' (the UPR page words it 'the All-Ukrainian Agrarian Congress elected Pavlo Skoropadsky the Hetman'); 'the Austro-Hungarian and German forces welcomed the coup' and 'the real power in the country belonged to the German staff headed by general Eichhorn'. Colour and dossier continue (same state, new regime). [Reviewer-fix eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: quotation replaced by the Ukrainian State page's own wording; the date 29 April is the page's.]

1918, December: the Directorate overthrows the Hetmanate and restores the Ukrainian People's Republic. The page: 'Skoropadsky abdicated his position as Hetman on 14 December, as the Ukrainian People's Army took Kyiv'; 'the Directorate toppled the Ukrainian State and re-established the Ukrainian People's Republic'. The UPR page gives 14 December (infobox) and 19 December (body) for the restoration.
1919, 3 January: the Red Army takes Kharkiv. The Ukrainian-Soviet War page: 'On January 3, the Red Army took Kharkov.' Mirror of ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic /ledger/6.

region.text: the West Ukrainian People's Republic, Eastern Galicia

ledger.note: 1919, 22 January: the republic and the West Ukrainian People's Republic unite. The page: 'on 22 January the two states officially united' (Unification Act, 1919 section); the Cliopatria 1919 shape is this united claim.

1919, January: the Red Army takes Poltava and Yekaterinoslav. The Ukrainian-Soviet War page: 'On January 20 the Soviet Army took Poltava' and 'On January 26 Dybenko took Yekaterinoslav'. Mirror of ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic /ledger/7.

region.text: the front zone: Volhynia and Podillia, the part of Ukraine the Bolsheviks had not taken 'by early 1920' (UPR page: 'except of Volhynia and western Podillia'); the Kiev offensive page: the UPR 'controlled only a small sliver of land near the territory administered by Poland'

ledger.note: 1919, 5 February: the Bolsheviks take Kyiv and the long fight for Ukraine begins. The page: 'On 5 February, the Bolshevik troops captured Kyiv' (1919 section). The contest now covers only the front zone (Volhynia and Podillia, where the UPR, the Poles and the Bolsheviks kept fighting to 1921); the land the Bolsheviks took in 1919 is carried by the loss events of January-March 1919, Eastern Galicia by the July 1919 loss to Poland. [Reviewer-fix eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: was the whole claimed shape; narrowed to the front zone because the losses are now events.]

1919, 5 February: the Bolsheviks take Kyiv again. The page: 'On 5 February, the Bolshevik troops captured Kyiv' (1919 section); the Ukrainian-Soviet War page puts the Directorate's move to Vinnytsia on 2 February. Mirror of ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic /ledger/8.

minus.text: Ukraine east of the Riga line, without Galicia and Volhynia (Poland), Northern Bukovina and Budjak (Romania) and Carpathian Ruthenia (Czechoslovakia)

region.text: the rest of Eastern and central Ukraine (same region as ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic /ledger/10)

ledger.note: 1919, March: the Bolsheviks overrun the rest of central and eastern Ukraine. The Ukrainian-Soviet War page: the Directorate moved to Proskurov around 6 March, 'yielding most of Polissia and Podillia to the Bolsheviks'; Hryhoriv's forces took Kherson on 2 March and Chernihiv fell on 12 January; the page dates no other town. The region is the researcher's reading, the same as the Soviet mirror. The Directorate held Kamianets-Podilskyi from the summer (UPR page: 'was able to establish its new temporary capital in Kamianets-Podilskyi'), which the Soviet dossier does not mirror.

region.text: the West Ukrainian People's Republic, Eastern Galicia

ledger.note: 1919, 18 July: Poland takes Eastern Galicia. The Polish-Ukrainian War page: the Ukrainian Galician Army was 'pushed back to the line of the Zbruch river on 16-18 July, after which ZUNR was occupied by Poland' and 'Poland won the disputed territory on 18 July 1919'. The UPR page sets the Galician Army's defeat and retreat to the confluence of the Dniester and the Zbruch in the paragraph of late May 1919 (the Poles took Lutsk on 15 May; an armistice on 24 May) and says the April 1920 Treaty of Warsaw 'established the Polish-Ukrainian border along the Zbruch'; the July date is the Polish-Ukrainian War page's. Counterpart second-polish-republic has no dossier yet.

region.text: the front zone: Volhynia and Podillia, the part of Ukraine the Bolsheviks had not taken 'by early 1920' (UPR page: 'except of Volhynia and western Podillia'); the Kiev offensive page: the UPR 'controlled only a small sliver of land near the territory administered by Poland'

ledger.note: 1921, 18 March: the Peace of Riga closes the fighting for the UPR. The page: 'On 18 March 1921, the Polish government signed the Peace of Riga'; the Civil War page says it 'split disputed territories in Belarus and Ukraine between Poland and Soviet Russia/Soviet Ukraine'. [Reviewer-fix eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: region narrowed to the same front zone as the contest_start.]

1921: the Ukrainian People's Republic ends as a state on Ukrainian soil. The page: 'the republic's government continued its activities in exile' (infobox: government-in-exile 1921-1992); the land passes to the Ukrainian SSR and, in the west, to Poland.

wars.name: Ukrainian-Soviet War
wars.outcome: The Bolsheviks took Kyiv in the winter of 1918, were driven out on 1 March 1918 with German help, and took it again on 5 February 1919; the Peace of Riga (18 March 1921) left the UPR without land and its government in exile.
wars.note: The pages disagree on the first fall of Kyiv: 26 January 1918 (Russian Civil War page) against the day of the 9 February treaty (UPR page). The 1919 shape is the claim; the front is not on the pages. [Reviewer-fix eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: the ledger now has the Soviet gains as loss events (Jan 1918, Feb 1918, Jan-Mar 1919); the contest events cover only the Volhynia-Podillia front, and the war zone keeps the whole 1919 claim as the land fought over.]

wars.name: Polish-Soviet War (UPR as Poland's ally)
wars.outcome: On 22 April 1920 'Ukrainian representative Andriy Livytskyi signed the Treaty of Warsaw'; on 25 April 'Polish troops supported by two Ukrainian divisions' attacked. The Peace of Riga followed on 18 March 1921.
wars.note: Territorial results belong to the Second Polish Republic and Soviet dossiers; the page names no zone for the UPR itself. The Polish-Ukrainian War of 1918-19 against the West Ukrainian People's Republic is a section on the page whose dates were read in the eu-17-b repair: the Polish-Ukrainian War page gives 1 November 1918 to 18 July 1919 (see the loss of Eastern Galicia).

certainty.note: Claims and shifting fronts; the only line on the pages is the 'preliminary demarcation line with the Russian SFSR' of 1918, which the page does not place.

notes:
Pages: 4 (budget 1-2): the UPR page and the Ukrainian State page (Cliopatria's Wikipedia field) are the budget; the Russian Civil War and Brest-Litovsk pages were opened for the russian-republic dossier and are reused for the dates they give.

Scope: Cliopatria has one 1919 shape under the Name 'Ukrainian People's Republic' but its Wikipedia field is 'Ukrainian State' (the 1918 Hetmanate). This dossier covers the Ukrainian state from the Third Universal (20 November 1917) to the Peace of Riga (18 March 1921) and records the Hetmanate as a regime of the same state (two rename events); a reviewer who prefers two states should split 29 April-14 December 1918 into 'Ukrainian State', which would need a new slug and colour.

Needs a dossier from another group: the West Ukrainian People's Republic (Eastern Galicia, November 1918 to 1919), merged on 22 January 1919; the Crimean Regional Government (1918, 'dependent on Ukraine' per the Ukrainian State page); the Don Republic and Kuban People's Republic on the east border; Belarusian People's Republic on the north (Ukrainian State page).

Not settled: (1) effective control in 1919-21 (the 1919 shape is a claim; the 1920 keyframe is a minimal radius around the temporary capitals); (2) the page's sentence that 'by early 1920 controlled most of the Ukrainian territory except of Volhynia and western Podillia' has an unclear subject in the summary I read, so it is not used; (3) the day of the first Bolshevik capture of Kyiv (26 January vs 9 February 1918); (4) the Directorate's restoration date: 14 December (infobox) or 19 December 1918 (body); the infobox also gives 13 November for the Directorate's formation while the body says 15 November; (5) the UPR page's de facto autonomy date: 23 June (infobox) vs 24 June 1917 (body); (6) the UPR's Wikipedia field: Cliopatria gives 'Ukrainian State', the dossier uses 'Ukrainian People's Republic'. Gazetteer names to add: none beyond the ones used (Mazyr, Kamyanets-Podilskyy, Vinnytsya, Khmelnytskyy and Rivne resolve).

Repair eu-17-b, 2026-10-31: (a) the Crimea subtraction (reviewer) is redundant in the gazetteer (Ukraine intersect Crimea is 0 cells) but stays so the text and the correction agree; (b) loss events added for the Soviet gains (mirrors of ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic /ledger/1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 10) and the loss of Eastern Galicia to second-polish-republic (18 July 1919); (c) the 1919 keyframe is now adjust (shape unchanged); (d) the contests cover the Volhynia-Podillia front only; (e) the /ledger/5 quotation is the Ukrainian State page's own; (f) not done: a loss of Kharkiv in December 1917 (the Soviet dossier's found event, /ledger/0, has no mirror here; the pages I read date it only by inference) and a Volhynia cession to Poland (extent not on the pages). Pages opened: Ukrainian-Soviet War, Polish-Ukrainian War, Kiev offensive (1920), Ukrainian State, Ukrainian People's Republic (all re-read for the repair).
